pr.title: Resurrect arr-flatten@1.1.0: replace with Array.prototype.flat (or a small loop)
pr.body:
## 🪦 arr-flatten@1.1.0 → Replace route

**Why this package:** risk 51/100, status **dormant**.
- No release for 9.4 years
- Imported at 1 site in 1 file

**Coroner's verdict:** A maintained replacement exists: Array.prototype.flat (or a small loop). Flatten nested arrays without the unmaintained arr-flatten. 2 candidates will be proven against the original before any change is kept.

### What changed
- Added `graveyard/shims/arr-flatten.cjs`: A modern loop that keeps holes as undefined, like the original
- Rewrote 1 import in 1 file: `src/cart.js`
- Removed `arr-flatten` from package.json and package-lock.json
- The public API of this project is unchanged: callers keep the same function names and arguments.

### Proof
fast-check generated inputs and ran each one through **both** the original `arr-flatten@1.1.0` and the new code. Every output had to be deep-equal (or both had to throw the same error type).

| Property | Runs | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| flattens nested and sparse arrays the same way | 500 | ✅ agree |

500 generated inputs, seed `20261031`, 64 ms. Ran in a Node.js permission-model sandbox: read-only file access, no child processes, empty environment.

#### Attempts
1. ❌ **flat-infinity**: Array.prototype.flat(Infinity). Rejected after 1 input.
   Counterexample `[[,]]`: original returns `[undefined]`, candidate returns `[]`.
2. ✅ **loop-keep-holes**: A modern loop that keeps holes as undefined, like the original. Agreed on all 500 inputs.

### Replay test (stays in the repo)
40 recorded cases in `graveyard/proofs/arr-flatten.golden.json`, replayed by `graveyard/proofs/arr-flatten.proof.test.js` with `node --test`: ✅ pass. They keep guarding the behaviour after the original package is gone.

Project tests (`npm test`): ✅ pass

### Risk note
- Equivalence is proven on generated inputs within the documented API, not on every possible value. Flatten nested arrays without the unmaintained arr-flatten.
- Array.prototype.flat drops holes in sparse arrays; the original turns them into undefined, so this loop does too.

### Provenance
- Original: `arr-flatten@1.1.0` (installed copy, matching the lockfile version)
- Integrity: `sha512-L3hKV5R/p5o81R7O02IGnwpDmkp6E982X…`
- Licence: MIT (no original code is copied)
- Recipe: `arr-flatten-native`, candidate `loop-keep-holes`

### Reviewer checklist
- [ ] The rewritten imports are the only call sites
- [ ] The risk note matches how this project uses the package
- [ ] CI passes

_Opened by Graveyard Shift. The Coroner chose the route, the Surgeon made the change, the proof decided. A human reviews and merges; nothing is published automatically. After merge, a Warden keeper bot watches this package for new advisories._
